advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that calls add_dependency twice on an escalated pair and asserts the SECOND (idempotent no-op) call still returns the redirect record.
evidence: Diff added `return redirect_record` replacing bare `return` on the idempotent branch.
search of tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_adddep.py for 'idempotent' / 'already exist' / 'is_active_link' returns no matches — no test relinks an existing escalated pair.
test_add_dependency_returns_the_redirect_record_when_it_escalates (line 543) writes tickets fresh and links once, hitting only the write branch at line 290, not the no-op branch at 277.
advisory.finding: The newly-added idempotent no-op return path (`return redirect_record` at src/rebar/graph/_links.py:277) has no test. All added tests exercise the fresh-write branch (line 290); none re-links an already-escalated pair to confirm the record is still returned when the link already exists. A regression that reverted line 277 to a bare `return` (dropping to None) would go undetected even though the diff's own comment claims 'parity with the pre-fix behavior' for this path.
scenarios: An agent or reconciler relinks an already-recorded escalated pair (leaf-a -> epic-b); the second call takes the idempotent no-op path.
A future refactor drops the return on line 277, silently returning None so the MCP tool reports plain 'ok' for an escalated-but-already-present edge.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test: after the first escalated add_dependency('leaf-a','epic-b',...), call it again with the same args and assert the returned record is non-None and equals the first record's original/resolved pairs (covering the no-op branch at _links.py:277).
